title: Roof and platform work: the licence questions still open
moduleTitle: Optional add-on: high-risk work and platform licences
audience: Workers and supervisors who may be asked to work at height or on a platform. Optional add-on, taken alongside the main courses.
learningOutcomes: List the boom-length rules that are confirmed and the ones that are not.
Identify the South Australian points that are not confirmed.

instruction.heading: What is confirmed
instruction.body: Lesson 2 sets out the 11 metre boom-length rules that official pages state for New South Wales, Tasmania, the Northern Territory, Western Australia and the ACT, and Queensland's exclusion of platforms under 11 metres.

instruction.heading: South Australia
instruction.body: SafeWork SA's high risk work licence page (last updated 10 January 2024) does not list a WP class and gives no boom length. Whether South Australia requires a WP licence is not confirmed by an official source.

instruction.heading: The South Australian pressure equipment class
instruction.body: The same South Australian page lists a 'pressure equipment operation' licence class. The class name is confirmed; whether it covers high-pressure water jetting is not confirmed by an official source, so do not treat it as covering jetting.

instruction.heading: Victoria
instruction.body: Victoria's WP class is confirmed; its boom-length rule is not confirmed by an official source (see lesson 3).

instruction.heading: Before any roof work from a platform
instruction.body: Check the licence rule for the state and the boom length with the regulator before work. This add-on does not give the answer for every state.

procedure: Identify the state and the boom length.
Check the regulator's page for the licence rule and record its date.
Where a point is not confirmed, ask the regulator before work.

workedExamples.situation: A roof cleaner in South Australia proposes to use a boom-type platform for a roof job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can this lesson say whether a WP licence applies?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. SafeWork SA's page lists no WP class and gives no boom length, so whether a WP licence applies is not confirmed by an official source. Ask SafeWork SA before work.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a state's rule from a neighbouring state.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the rule for the state where the work is done.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Roof and platform work needs the licence and authority that apply in the state where the work is done. This add-on grants neither.

qualityStandard: Learner marks each unconfirmed point before answering a licence question.
documentationEvidence: State, boom length, regulator page and page date recorded before the job.
summary: Confirmed and unconfirmed points are kept separate.
South Australian WP and jetting positions are not confirmed.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which South Australian point is confirmed in this lesson?
options: South Australia requires a WP licence for any boom
The 'pressure equipment operation' class name appears on the SA licence page
Jetting needs the pressure equipment licence

officialReferences.title: High risk work licence (SA Government)
officialReferences.covers: Class list shows a 'pressure equipment operation' class and no WP class and no boom length.

officialReferences.title: High risk work licence (WorkSafe Victoria)
officialReferences.covers: Names the boom-type elevating work platform operation licence class; states the class without a boom length; scissor lifts do not need the WP licence. Does not state whether the class applies at any boom length.
